identity.spiritualSignificanceShort: Swaminarayan Akshardham is a modern BAPS mandir complex on the Yamuna in Delhi, inaugurated on 6 November 2005 — not an ancient temple. Beneath its central dome sits a 3.4 m murti of Swaminarayan in abhayamudra, surrounded by images of the sampradaya's lineage of gurus. Alongside darshan the complex runs ticketed exhibitions and an evening water show, and it is one of Delhi's most visited sites.

narrative.documentedHistory:
Swaminarayan Akshardham is a modern complex, not a historic temple. The project traces to a wish expressed by Yogiji Maharaj in 1968 for a grand mandir on the banks of the Yamuna. Construction ran from November 2000 to November 2005, and the mandir was inaugurated on 6 November 2005 by Pramukh Swami Maharaj. Roughly seven thousand carvers and three thousand volunteers worked on it.

The mandir is 43 m high, 96 m wide and 109 m long, built of Rajasthani pink sandstone and Italian Carrara marble and, following traditional guidelines, without ferrous metal. It carries 234 carved pillars and nine domes, and the Gajendra Pith plinth bears 148 life-sized carved elephants. Under the central dome is a 3.4 m murti of Swaminarayan in abhayamudra, surrounded by images of the sampradaya's gurus.

In December 2007 Guinness World Records recognised Akshardham as the world's largest comprehensive Hindu temple. The complex also contains the Yagnapurush Kund stepwell, the setting for a 24-minute multimedia water show, and three ticketed exhibitions on Hindu culture and the life of Swaminarayan.
narrative.architectureStyle: Traditional Hindu mandir architecture in Rajasthani pink sandstone and Italian Carrara marble, built without ferrous metal

visitingInfo.dressCode: Enforced. Upper wear must cover shoulders, chest, back and upper arms; lower wear must extend below the knees. Delhi Tourism notes that wraps are available against a refundable ₹100 deposit for visitors who arrive unsuitably dressed.
visitingInfo.entryRules: Open Tuesday to Sunday and closed every Monday. Entry to the mandir complex and mandir darshan is free; the exhibitions and the water show are separately ticketed. Entry rules are unusually strict: all electronic items — mobile phones, cameras, USB drives, music devices — are barred, as are weapons, umbrellas, luggage, toys, pets, food and drink, tobacco, alcohol and drugs, and drones. A free cloakroom operates from 10:00 am to gate closing, and deposited electronic items must be switched off. Smoking, alcohol and drugs, tobacco products, impolite behaviour and language, and pets are prohibited inside. Plan for a security check and allow time to deposit belongings before entering.
visitingInfo.photographyPolicy: Cameras and mobile phones may not be taken inside; visitors deposit them at the cloakroom. There is no visitor photography within the complex.
visitingInfo.officialContactNote: Confirm the day's timings, exhibition and water-show tickets and the current show time with the complex on +91-11-4344 2344 or at akshardham.com before travelling. The water show follows sunset and its time moves through the year. Address: NH 24, Pramukh Swami Maharaj Marg, New Delhi 110092.
